summary: The Model Context Protocol (MCP), released by Anthropic in November 2024, has exploded into the standard way AI agents connect to external tools and data, reaching roughly 97 million monthly SDK downloads by December 2025 and becoming a founding project of the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation. MCP turns capable-but-isolated coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex into agents that can actually act on real systems — browsers, repos, databases, and SaaS apps. The ecosystem now spans aggregator platforms, gateways, and thousands of individual servers.
ecosystem_note: Individual MCP servers each expose one tool or service (e.g., GitHub or Playwright), aggregators bundle hundreds or thousands of integrations behind a single managed endpoint (e.g., Composio, Smithery), and gateways/proxies sit in front of many servers to add auth, routing, governance, and observability for production use (e.g., Cloudflare, Kong, Zuplo).

tools.name: GitHub MCP Server
tools.connects_to: GitHub repositories, issues, pull requests, Actions, code search, and file contents
tools.pricing_paid: Free; usage governed by existing GitHub plan limits (Free/Team/Enterprise)
strengths: Deep repo, issue, and PR automation
Remote hosted option plus local Docker image
Massive install base across all major agents
tools.best_for: Agents that read, write, and manage code and project workflows on GitHub

tools.name: Playwright MCP Server
tools.connects_to: Live web browsers for navigation, DOM interaction, form filling, scraping, and automated testing
strengths: One of the most-starred and most-installed servers
tools.best_for: Browser automation, end-to-end testing, and web research by agents

tools.name: Composio
tools.connects_to: 1,500+ apps and 50,000+ actions (Gmail, Slack, Linear, Notion, Jira, GitHub, etc.) through one managed endpoint
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier available; usage-based paid plans and enterprise pricing
strengths: Consolidates many integrations behind one auth layer
tools.best_for: Teams wanting hundreds of SaaS integrations without managing individual servers

tools.name: Filesystem MCP Server
tools.connects_to: Local file system — reading, writing, searching, and editing files within allowed directories
tools.best_for: Giving agents controlled access to local project files

tools.name: Figma MCP Server (Dev Mode)
tools.connects_to: Figma design files, frames, components, and Dev Mode metadata for design-to-code workflows
tools.pricing_paid: Requires Figma plan with Dev Mode (paid seats); server itself free
strengths: Extracts layout, styles, and component structure
Popular for Cursor and Claude Code UI generation
tools.best_for: Turning Figma designs into production front-end code with agents

tools.name: Cloudflare MCP Server / Remote MCP
tools.connects_to: Cloudflare Workers, hosted remote MCP servers, Workers AI, D1, R2, and OAuth-secured remote deployment
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; Workers Paid from $5/month and usage-based pricing
strengths: Deploy and host remote MCP servers with OAuth
First-party tooling for building MCP servers
tools.best_for: Deploying production, remotely hosted MCP servers at scale

tools.name: Smithery
tools.connects_to: A registry and marketplace of thousands of MCP servers with one-click install and hosted deployment
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid hosting and usage plans
tools.best_for: Discovering, installing, and hosting MCP servers quickly

tools.name: Docker MCP Toolkit / Catalog
tools.connects_to: Containerized MCP servers run in isolated Docker environments, with a curated catalog and MCP Gateway
tools.pricing_paid: Free with Docker Desktop; Docker Business/Team plans for enterprise
tools.best_for: Running MCP servers securely in isolated containers

tools.name: mcp.so
tools.connects_to: A large community directory indexing thousands of MCP servers and clients for discovery
tools.best_for: Browsing and discovering available MCP servers across the ecosystem

tools.name: Context7 MCP Server
tools.connects_to: Up-to-date, version-specific library documentation and code examples injected into agent context
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid plans for higher usage via Upstash
strengths: Very popular with Cursor and Claude Code users
tools.best_for: Giving coding agents accurate, current library documentation

tools.name: Kong (Konnect) MCP Gateway
tools.connects_to: Existing APIs and MCP servers behind Kong's API gateway with auth, rate limiting, and observability
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source Kong Gateway free; Konnect paid plans and enterprise pricing
strengths: Turns existing APIs into MCP tools
tools.best_for: Enterprises exposing existing APIs to agents with governance

tools.name: Zuplo MCP Gateway
tools.connects_to: Federates multiple remote MCP servers (GitHub, Slack, Stripe, internal) behind one secured gateway endpoint
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; usage-based and enterprise paid plans
strengths: Single federated endpoint for many MCP servers
Productionization: auth, routing, and policy control
Works across Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and VS Code
Fast setup for internal + external servers
tools.best_for: Federating and securing multiple MCP servers in production
